attrs.evidence: governance/brief_identity.mjs (--check) wired into governance/make_review_pack.sh before the brief is copied, plus IDENTITY.txt written into the pack from the same derivation. Measured against the stale P4.7.4 brief: BRIEF-IDENTITY FAIL naming all three lines.
attrs.statement: A REVIEW BRIEF IS EVIDENCE, SO ITS NUMBERS ARE DERIVED. The P4.7.4 brief's header read `package bpkg-d43546...09ee18e40f5   53 files` while blind-package.json, blind-run.json and the BLIND-PACKAGE gate all said `bpkg-d43546...f6490e1d211` over 54 files: the digest PREFIX was right because it was copied from a console line truncated at eighty columns, THE TAIL WAS COMPLETED BY HAND, and the file count was carried over from the previous round's brief. The pack's MANIFEST.sha256 verified perfectly around it and the executable record was correct throughout, so no experiment integrity was affected -- which is exactly why it is worth a law: a manifest authenticates BYTES and not the prose beside them, and the brief is the document a reviewer reads before deciding whether to trust the tree at all. This project already forbids hand-typed law counts and hand-typed gate tallies; the round brief was the last place a number was still being typed. `brief_identity.mjs` DERIVES the release, package and run identity block from the three records, refuses to print one when those records disagree with each other, and `make_review_pack.sh` REFUSES TO BUILD a pack whose brief does not contain the block verbatim.
